# Audio Design

## Full cast, real foley

> status: ratified (D-0001, D-0035)

High-production, audiobook-like: fully voiced characters over rich foley, with the
narrator bracketing each episode. The sound is the show's visual budget.

## Music as punctuation and mood

> status: ratified (D-0039)

Very clear musical choices used two ways: punctuation (fixed signatures at beginning
and end) and mood/tone within the episode — danger, rising tension, excitement,
romance — as a consistent, recognizable lexicon the listener learns.

## The acoustic palette

> status: ratified (D-0023, D-0024)

From the author's own touchstone analyses: acoustic, pre-industrial instrumentation
in the Frieren/Inuyasha tradition — Celtic/Northern folk textures (pipes, whistle,
fiddle, frame drum, hurdy-gurdy drone) crossed with the traditional-orchestral
gravity of the Inuyasha score; the courage to hold silence — wind, fire-crackle,
boots in mud — instead of wall-to-wall scoring.

## Motif sketches

> status: provisional (D-0072)

Approved directionally: the ruling order sounds rigid and mathematical (metronomic
pulses, dead-air sterility, the scratch of quills, chains drawn taut); the wild Wyrd
sounds organic and unpredictable (breathy woodwinds, erratic deep percussion,
subsonic ground-tones); the hearth sounds warm and small (a single fiddle or plucked
string under found-family quiet). Regional soundworlds follow the biome cultures in
[[regions]].

## The chorus in the mix

> status: ratified (D-0069)

The protagonist's absorbed multitude has explicit sound-design implications. Working
sketches (provisional D-0072): under heavy casting, other voices phase into hers —
layered breaths and unison speech panned just off-center; small tells leak through in
quiet moments (a borrowed breathing rhythm, a loom-tap of the fingers, an accent
sliding for one word); a full firewall collapse is an audio set-piece — one throat
carrying an argument among several dead speakers. The apprentice's discovery of the
depth of what she is should be carried by sound before it is ever explained in
dialogue.

## Casting as labor

> status: provisional (D-0072)

Magic never gets a "whoosh." Proof-speech sounds like work: controlled breath
starting to fray, sweat-and-wool closeness, a nosebleed hitting slate, the anchor's
grip keeping a swaying body upright. The scariest sound in the show is a very calm
voice under enormous strain.

## Production voice baselines

> status: ratified (D-0221)

Jane is the canonical Enfys render voice and the default for new Enfys scene
renders. The durable tracked alias is `enfys_jane_voice_probe`; raw provider voice
IDs stay outside the repository and must never be committed or logged. Earlier
Enfys lanes, including Michelle, Clare, Welsh carried, and E3, are historical
comparison evidence unless a later author ruling reopens them.

## Aphorisms as acoustic identity
> status: ratified (D-0090)

Because the show is heard and not seen, the belief systems cannot lean on a visible holy
symbol; their repeated aphorisms and key phrases do that work instead. A creed's
recurring line — spoken in a fixed cadence, often over a signature texture — becomes its
acoustic logo, giving the listener callbacks and a steady orientation on each faction's
values. The empire's scribes, the native animists, and the working poor should each be
identifiable by phrase and delivery before any name is spoken. The specimens live in
[[in-world-texts]].
